before.title: Document PR187/208 performance and organize GPU benchmark history
before.body:
The PR187/208 measurements and storage qualifications were spread across task notes. Add a GPU performance entry point, a dated hardware inventory, and a history page while preserving the existing read/staging and calibration-plus-integration reports.

The consolidated report records:
- Ada 016 A/B/C results: raw paired loop changes below 1%, and +10.17% for four-BD warm calibration B/A, largely localized before first-event delivery.

Compact evidence includes sample arrays, source hashes, and hardware observations. Both runtime PRs have merged; this change records the investigation's outcome and limitations.

Validation: checked 350 sample-statistic sets and paired comparisons against saved samples, all 66 relative links (including four anchors), JSON parsing, inventory consistency, and Git whitespace checks. Repository commit hooks passed. Documentation only; no new GPU jobs or runtime changes.

before.title: Deliver transitions in order and make run.steps() work on GPU ranks
before.body:
## Motivation

Works toward #153 (P1). Base is `features/psana2-gpu`; design in #172;
stacked on #241 (merged).

On GPU ranks every transition in a packet was delivered **ahead of the
packet's own events**. On the final packet that put `EndRun` before the run's
last events, and both `Run.events()` and `_steps_impl` return on `EndRun` —
so those events were silently lost (a final packet of two events plus
Disable/EndStep/EndRun delivered 0 of 2). Every earlier acceptance run was
capped by `max_events`, so none reached `EndRun` and none could see it.
Separately, `RunParallel.steps()` returned without yielding on GPU ranks, so
`run.steps()` did not work there at all (GPU-140-03).

The change:

- **Transitions are queued and released by timestamp between events**, so each
  goes out after the events it follows and before those recorded after it.
- **Each packet's events carry a `StepScope(run, index, begin_ts)`**, decided
  by timestamp in `gpu_plan.py` before the generation advances, so events
  before a trailing `BeginStep` keep the step they were recorded in
  (GPU-148-01). Exposed to kernels as `batch.step_scope`.
- **`run.steps()` / `step.events()` work on GPU BD ranks**, serial and MPI.
- **`BeginStep` no longer drains the execution pool** — each subbatch has its
  own scope, so the next step's work is admitted while the previous step's is
  in flight. Only `EndRun` drains; constants are uploaded once per run.
- **A packet is decoded once**: `_process_batch` hands its transition list to
  `_handle_steps` instead of the latter re-decoding the SMD batch (on the MPI
  BD path, the whole batch, L1s included).

**Not supported — each enforced by a raise, none silently mishandled:**

| Limit | Enforced at |
| --- | --- |
| One step scope per packet: a `BeginStep` may not fall *between* a packet's events. Holds because the EB breaks its GPU batch on `BeginStep`. Narrower than Design 1's subbatch splitting, which does not exist. | `gpu_plan.py:137` |
| One GPU view may carry transitions per packet (MPI always has one; bulk reads require one). | `gpu_events.py:1379` |
| GPU events strictly increasing in timestamp; no event shares a timestamp with a transition. | `gpu_plan.py:94`, `:98` |
| A transition's dgrams share one aligned timestamp; history arrives ordered. | `gpu_plan.py:70`, `:85` |
| Planner and dispatcher agree on the step generation. | `gpu_events.py:1342` |

**Deferred against #153, deliberately** (so this PR does not close it):
the remainder/close matrix (GPU-149-04, "subject to API review" — a `Step`
shares the parent iterator exactly as the CPU path does); mid-packet step
splitting; Enable/chunkinfo rollover on the non-bulk reader
(`gpu_kvikio_read.py:335-339` still reads the mutable latest-file handle);
the fragmentation / scheduling-cost / high-water measurements; an explicit
cross-slot overlap test.

## How to test the behavior?

```
# The case that matters: uncapped, so the run reaches EndRun.
# MPI, 4 ranks = 1 smd0 + 1 EB + 2 BD, one A100, mfx100852324 run 77
SBATCH_ACCOUNT=lcls:prjdat21 SBATCH_QOS=normal sbatch \
  --export=ALL,PS_STEPS_DATASET=77,PS_STEPS_NO_CAP=1 \
  validation/gpu-steps-20261103/run.sbatch
#   expect: MPI_STEPS_RESULT {'counts': [3, 3], 'total': 3000,
#                             'per_step': [[500, 500, 500], [500, 500, 500]]}
#   (job 44509184 at a29258975). Before this branch the trailing step was cut
#   short and the run never reached EndRun.

# Serial counterpart, same run: run.events() count and run.steps() per step
python3 validation/gpu-steps-20261103/serial_events.py
#   expect: SERIAL77 events=3000 expected=3000
#           SERIAL77 per_step=[1000, 1000, 1000] total=3000  SERIAL77_PASS

# Memory pressure mid-packet must lose nothing and keep order
PS_PRESSURE_BATCH=200 PS_PRESSURE_GB=0.25 PS_PRESSURE_STREAMS=4 python3 validation/gpu-steps-20261103/pressure_events.py
#   expect: 3000 of 3000, per_step [1000, 1000, 1000], recoveries > 0
#   (job 43402513: 999 recoveries)

# Suites (A100): 1393 unit, 556 integration, 0 failed  (job 44509177)
pytest psana/psana/tests/gpu/unit psana/psana/tests/test_utils_service.py
pytest psana/psana/tests/gpu/integration
#   trailing-BeginStep scope on device:
#   test_gpu_steps_device.py::test_events_before_a_trailing_beginstep_are_stamped_with_the_old_step

# Recorded CPU tests: 42 passed, 4 skipped on the run_psana_tests.yaml group;
# run_steps.py identical before/after at 5 ranks/1 EB and 7 ranks/2 EBs (job 43343819).
# These tests do not cover C1: the CPU Step-parent lifetime regression remains unresolved.
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Did you update `CHANGELOG.md` with your changes? — **N/A: this repo has no `CHANGELOG.md`** (neither #241 nor #262 touched one).
- [x] Does the PR clearly describe the problem and the solution?
- [ ] Do all GitHub Actions checks pass on this PR? — `run_psana_tests.yaml`'s group passes locally (42/4); will confirm once the Action runs.
- [ ] Does the PR use "Fix #XXX" notation? — **Intentionally not.** Five checklist items of #153 are deferred (listed above), so this is "works toward #153", not a fix.


## Perlmutter performance follow-up

Full report, frozen running/analysis scripts, paired CSV/plot, checksums, and
audit records are preserved separately in https://github.com/slac-lcls/lcls2/pull/314 (draft). The
four evidence-package commits are reverted here to keep this implementation
PR focused; no production changes are reverted.

Compared baseline `11e4a13b541e2aefbfcb7168ab4d2040e2bcd4ba` with PR head
`acfd029a8d27898b5f165e02facd3c3bbc9c4ad2`, not later documentation/base commits.
Perlmutter job 61375111 completed 12 preflights and 48 timed samples: four
alternating B/H, H/B pairs per case, all timed samples using the same 10,000
Run51 events. Fresh local release builds; one physical A100, one stream per BD;
BD1/BD2 share that GPU with one/two BD workers; batch size 20, 8 GB per BD;
raw Jungfrau GPU workload without calibration/full-image D2H; bulk reads with
KvikIO CPU fallback, no GDS.

Median paired event-loop throughput change (positive = faster head):

| Workload | BD1 | BD2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GPU events | +0.00% | +0.98% |
| CPU events | +0.40% | +0.74% |
| CPU nested steps | -0.48% | +0.80% |

**Accept the scoped Run51 performance screen, not statistical equivalence or
merge approval.**
Pair extrema across cases span -3.28% to +6.82%; GPU BD1 has a 5.31 percentage-point
head-first/head-second gap. All GPU samples completed sustained execution, but
BD2 throughput drift, uncontrolled storage/cache/reclaim state, and unavailable
Lustre/PSI telemetry limit attribution. MPI-wall/startup timings are separate;
these results do not prove end-to-end equivalence or resolve the SDF/Weka slowdown.

**Functional readiness remains separate:** C1 (CPU Step-parent lifetime) is
blocking/unfixed; nested loops retain the parent and do not test it. The independent Perlmutter Run77
multi-step/EndRun follow-up remains deferred; earlier SDF Run77 validation is
recorded above. This capped Run51 prefix does not exercise EndRun. R1 whitespace, R2 GPU parent-lifetime documentation, and parser
optimization #310 remain nonblocking follow-ups.
